candidates.exact_span: Input pollutant geometric mean concentration as micro-gram per liter (ug/l or ppb) unless other unit is specified for the parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether compliance comparisons must use a geometric mean (and over what reporting window) can change the numeric value compared against an applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) but the DL is greater than MQL, input "1/2 DL" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A different reading of when DL exceeds MQL, or whether 1/2 DL must be used, changes the numeric effluent value used for limit comparison and how sub-MQL/non-detect results are classified.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) and the DL is smaller than MQL, no data is inputted.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a reported value is treated as no data versus a substitute numeric input changes both applicable limit evaluation and whether the case is documented no-data, missing evidence, or unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: If a less than MQL vakue is reported, input either the reported value or "0" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The permissive 'either ... or "0"' choice can yield different effluent concentrations for compliance comparison and different semantics for below-MQL reported results.
If permit compliance is determined through instream waste concentration, different interpretations of this formula or its inputs change the derived enforceable concentration used for comparison.

candidates.exact_span: F = Fraction of stream allow ed for mixing (see "Procedures for Implementing NPDES Permits in New Mexico")
candidates.computation_change_reason: The applicable mixing fraction F directly alters calculated instream waste concentration and therefore which numeric limit applies or whether a measurement exceeds it.

candidates.exact_span: Qa = Critical low flow of stream at discharge point expressed as the 4Q3 or harmonic mean flow for human health criteria
candidates.computation_change_reason: Choosing 4Q3 versus harmonic mean for Qa changes dilution assumptions and can change the calculated limit or compliance outcome.

candidates.exact_span: TSS = Total suspended solids concentration found in receiving stream (or in effluent for intermittent stream)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether TSS must be taken from the receiving stream or from effluent for an intermittent stream affects dissolved-metal conversion and may also change which monitoring location or discharge-condition requirement is applicable.
Different interpretation of the total-to-dissolved conversion factor changes the dissolved criteria value against which effluent metals are compared.
This step converts dissolved criteria to total-metal enforceable limits; a different reading changes the applicable numeric discharge limit.
The stream dissolved-value entry of 0 for Chromium III may be read as a zero limit, a placeholder, or inapplicable; that changes whether a numeric compliance comparison is possible.

candidates.exact_span: If Stream pH < 6.5, enter 750 in cell O113
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the pH condition is met determines whether the acute aluminum criterion uses the hardness formula or the fixed 750 ug/l value, changing the applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: If Stream pH < 6.5, enter 87 in cell P113
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the pH condition is met determines whether the chronic aluminum criterion uses the hardness formula or the fixed 87 ug/l value, changing the applicable limit.
The hardness-dependent correction factor for acute cadmium directly changes the calculated enforceable limit.
The hardness-dependent correction factor for chronic cadmium directly changes the calculated enforceable limit.

candidates.exact_span: STEP 2:            INPUT AMBIENT AND EFFLUENT DATA
candidates.computation_change_reason: If this calculation step is operative permit methodology, it implies ambient and effluent data must be obtained; interpretation of what inputs are required affects which monitoring obligations are established as applicable.
